comment: Every number the player feels, with its reasoning beside it. `comment` and `*Comment` keys are stripped when the file is loaded. A magic number in the Kotlin is a bug: put it here. Figures marked (filled in) are our own judgement where no source gives a number; the historiker's pre-check is docs/pruefer/historiker_vorpruefung_1939.md.

units.comment: One piece on the map is a division. How it fights (docs/GEFECHT.md): fire is what it brings against men in the open and antiTank against armour, as attacks a day; armoured is the share of it that is armour (0 to 1), which decides how much of an enemy's fire and how much of his antiTank it draws; hold is how many attacks a day it can take under cover while it defends, and drive the same while it attacks -- past that every attack tells nearly four times as often; plate is how thick its armour is and pierce how thick a plate its guns go through; front is the room it takes in the line. speed is kilometres a day on good roads; cost is factory-days; manpower is thousands of men for the division and its slice of corps and army troops; fuel is what it burns a day when it moves or fights. The proportions follow what the arms could do in 1939-41 (an infantry division held a line and could not break one without odds or guns; a tank division broke lines and could hardly be hurt by infantry's anti-tank rifles and 37 mm guns); the numbers themselves are ours (filled in).

INF.comment: Infantry on foot with horse-drawn guns: 86 of Germany's 104 divisions in 1939. Holds; breaks nothing alone.

ARM.comment: An armoured division: about 300 tanks. Dear, thirsty, and it breaks a line.

MOT.comment: Motorised infantry and the light divisions: keeps up with the tanks and holds what they take.

CAV.comment: Cavalry, which fought dismounted; quick, thin.

MTN.comment: Mountain troops: no penalty in hills and mountains.

GAR.comment: Fortress troops, militia and second-line reserves: hold a line, cannot take one.

terrain.comment: What the ground does. frontage is the room for divisions in one battle there (a division's `front` is 2, so open country has room for eight a side); move multiplies speed; defense multiplies how much the defender can take under cover; attack multiplies the attacker's fire and drive, by kind of unit (a kind not named takes `all`). A region's terrain is the kind that covers most of it.

combat.comment: A battle is fought a day at a time for one region, between the divisions attacking it and those in it (docs/GEFECHT.md; the design precedent is the land combat of the Hearts of Iron series -- how it works, not its names or numbers). Each side puts into the line what the frontage has room for; the rest wait. Every division in the line fires on the enemy's line; what a division can take under cover (hold when it defends, drive when it attacks) is hit seldom, what comes on top of that is hit often. Hits wear down organisation fast and strength slowly; a division whose organisation is spent falls back, or is lost if it has nowhere to go.
combat.flankFrontageComment: Each further region an attack comes from adds this share of the ground's frontage, up to two: an enemy struck from three sides faces twice the line.
combat.stackComment: More divisions than this on one side of one battle get in each other's way: each one more costs the whole side this share of its fire.
combat.overflowComment: The last division into the line may stand a little past the frontage; its side fires that much worse, and past this share it stays out.
combat.focusComment: This share of a division's fire falls on the enemy division nearest to breaking; the rest is spread along his line by frontage.
combat.hitComment: The chance that an attack tells: on a division still under cover, and on one that has more coming at it than it can take. The second is what breaks a line.
combat.perHitComment: What one hit costs a full division, of its organisation and of its strength. A division broken in battle has lost about a fifth of its men. (filled in)
combat.pierceComment: Fire on a division whose plate the shooter's guns cannot go through: with pierce at least three quarters of the plate, at least half, or less.
combat.unpiercedShockComment: A division the enemy's line cannot pierce shakes him more: its hits cost him this much more organisation.
combat.encircledComment: A defender with no friendly region to fall back to fights this much worse.
combat.breakOrgComment: Below this a division can no longer fight and falls back.
combat.attackMinOrgComment: A division this tired breaks off its attack and waits: an army that attacks until it is spent has nothing left to hold with.
combat.regroupDaysComment: After breaking off an attack a division needs this long before it can attack again.
combat.landingComment: Attacking from the sea onto a defended shore.
combat.landingFrontComment: How much frontage of an attack may come over a beach.
combat.fortCoverComment: And each level adds this share to what the defender can take under cover: concrete is cover.
combat.fortPerLevelComment: Each level of permanent fortification takes this share off the attacker's fire and drive: level 3, the Maginot Line's strong sectors, leaves him 58 percent. Each further direction of attack turns one level, never the last. The historiker's scale: 1 field works, 2 a light permanent line, 3 a heavy one.
combat.entrenchComment: A division that stays put digs in, up to this bonus on what it can take and what it fires.
combat.diceComment: The day's luck: a side's hits vary by this much either way, from the game's seed.
combat.surpriseComment: The side that opens a war fights better for its first weeks: the defender is not yet mobilised (Poland stood at two thirds on 1 September 1939; the Red Army in June 1941).

movement.comment: A division marches from one region's town to the next. Days = distance / (speed x terrain x roads x weather).
movement.friendlyRailComment: Inside one's own lines, away from the enemy, troops go by rail.

weather.comment: The east and the far north have a mud season and a hard winter (the rasputitsa of October-November and March-April; the winter of 1941-42). A region has them if it lies east of `mudEastOfLon` or north of `mudNorthOfLat`.
weather.winterAttackComment: Applies to the attacker. States in `winterHardy` (countries.json) are spared.

supply.comment: A division is supplied if its region is joined, through land its own side holds, to its capital or to a port its navy can reach. Cut off, it wastes away: this is what makes an encirclement kill.
supply.reinforcePerDayComment: Share of full strength a division out of battle gets back a day, if men and factories allow.
supply.depthPenaltyComment: An army far from home attacks worse: each region between it and its own country (or an ally's) takes this much off its attack, up to the maximum. The railheads did not keep up in Russia in 1941, nor in France in 1944. (filled in)
supply.occupationYieldComment: Share of a conquered region's factories and oil that works for the occupier. (filled in)

economy.comment: Factories make factory-days; a division costs factory-days and men. Oil makes fuel.
economy.manpowerPerMillionPerMonthComment: Thousands of recruits a month for each million people still under one's own control, at war. Germany's 79 million give about 170,000 a month; over five years ten million, which is the order of what it called up. (filled in)
economy.warEconomyPerYearComment: A state at war turns more of its industry to arms each year it fights, up to `warEconomyMax` (Germany's and Britain's output roughly doubled between 1940 and 1944).
economy.peaceEconomyComment: A state at peace arms at half pace.

sea.comment: Navies and air forces are one number per state for now (ROADMAP: fleets as pieces). A sea zone is ruled by whoever brings the most power to it from the bases he holds; power falls off with distance.
sea.dominanceComment: A side rules a zone when its power there is this many times the enemy's. Between the two it is contested.
sea.contestedLossComment: Share of a division lost crossing a contested sea.

diplomacy.capitulationDefaultComment: A state gives up when it has lost its capital and this share of its victory points; countries.json may name another share.
diplomacy.ultimatumRatioComment: An AI gives way to an ultimatum when the other's army is this many times its own and nobody at war stands with it.

ai.comment: How the computer plays. It gives the same orders a player gives.
ai.attackOddsComment: It attacks where a day of the battle would cost the defender this many times the organisation it costs the attacker; a state's `aggression` in countries.json scales it.
ai.stagingDaysComment: This long before a war its plan intends, a state masses on that frontier: Germany's divisions stood on the Danish and the Dutch border before the day, not after it.
ai.frontPerThreatComment: Divisions wanted in a front region for each point of enemy attack power next to it.
